parties.counterparty: Marshall & Ilsley Corporation, acting through its M&I Data Services division ("M&I")

plans.note: Cap at § 13.4 (p0207): M&I liability limited to fees paid in the 3 months before the event, plus a 1-year suit limitation with a carve-out only for collection of amounts due. Mutual consequential waiver § 13.2 (p0205); helpful enumerated direct damages § 13.1 (p0198-p0204); equitable relief preserved (p0206). Assess: effectively one-sided (Customer's termination fees expressly excluded from the cap per p0187/p0189), 3 months is very low, and no carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality/data breach or willful misconduct. p0304 is the negotiated-limitations construction clause. Do not double-flag the termination-fee quantum here.

Vendor indemnity present at § 14.2(B) (p0220): third-party US patent/copyright/trademark infringement, third-party claims re M&I systems, breach of M&I reps, discrimination/harassment, injury/death, and property/financial loss from M&I acts or omissions — meets the preferred position. Customer's mirror indemnity § 14.2(A) (p0219); note the § 6.6(B) hook and Customer-pays-enforcement-costs sentence. Procedures § 14.3 (p0221-p0225). Other Customer-side indemnities to check for breadth: ACH mutual indemnity p0114 with M&I's ACH liability narrowed to gross negligence/willful misconduct p0117; reliance-on-data indemnity p0270; TIN hold-harmless p0279.

No restraint on the businesses we may operate. Closest are use/field-of-use limits: § 21.7(B) (p0273) confines us to internal business purposes and bars reselling Services; § 23.5 (p0313) limits source-code use to internal processing and then-existing functionalities. These are conventional resale/scope limits, likely compliant. § 10.3(A) (p0183) is a purchase restriction handled under EXCLUSIVITY/MINCOMMIT, not here.

Responsive: § 10.3(A) (p0183) requires Customer for the whole 8-year Term to obtain from M&I all Services included in the Monthly Base Fee (Schedule 6.2) — a sole-source lock with no descope or partial-termination right, removing our freedom to buy elsewhere. Reinforced by § 21.10 (p0280) sweeping all Affiliate/subsidiary processing into the Agreement. Note asymmetry: §§ 3.1-3.2 (p0057-p0058) let M&I subcontract to Affiliates/third parties while we are locked in.

No MFN or most-favoured-pricing language; searches for most favored/favoured, no less favorable, comparable customers, lowest price and best pricing returned nothing. Pricing is Fee-Schedule driven with discounts at p0153 and then-current published rates in places (p0151, p0192). No MFN burden on us — nothing to flag; an MFN in our favour is an optional ask.

§ 22.14 (p0302): mutual, Term-limited bar on soliciting the other party's employees ('during the Term ... for any reason'). Mutuality and duration are acceptable; note the absence of a general-advertising / unsolicited-applicant carve-out and that 'employees' is unqualified.

Customer T4C exists at § 11.1 (p0187) but is heavily penalised: one year's notice plus a Termination for Convenience Fee of a REDACTED percentage of Estimated Remaining Value (p0039), plus unamortised Conversion costs and disposition Expenses, 50% due on notice, and expressly outside the § 13.4 cap. § 11.2(A) (p0189) imposes a Termination for Cause Fee even where we terminate under 11.1 without the notice formalities. Favourable offsets to preserve: p0190 (no fee on M&I default) and p0263 (penalty-free exit for unresolved Disaster). Also note M&I's unilateral 90-day partial withdrawal right § 10.2 (p0180-p0181).

No auto-renewal. § 2.2 (p0055): M&I must propose renewal 18 months pre-expiry, we respond within 6 months, and failing agreement we hold a unilateral option to extend 12 months at then-current terms on 5 months' notice. Term is 8 years from the Commencement Date (p0049). Mechanic favours us — do not flag; note only the long initial term and the notice choreography.

§ 22.1 (p0286) Wisconsin internal law; § 22.2 (p0287) exclusive venue in Milwaukee County and E.D. Wis. Courts rather than foreign arbitration, but Wisconsin is outside the accepted list (NY/DE/CA/E&W) and is M&I's home forum. Note references to an 'arbitrator' at p0298-p0299 and the § 15 escalation/continuity process (p0226, p0228) — confirm no binding arbitration is imported.

§ 22.4 (p0289): mutual consent (not unreasonably withheld), but Customer's only exception is a merger where the survivor becomes an affiliate of a $100MM+ financial institution and § 21.11 is satisfied, while M&I may assign freely on merger/asset sale or to a successor of the M&I Data Services division — asymmetric and no affiliate-assignment right for us. On change of control, § 21.11(B) (p0284) caps M&I's obligations to pre-CoC entities and prior 3-month volumes +25%; § 21.11(A) (p0282-p0283) puts new-Affiliate Conversion Expenses and to-be-agreed Conversion Fees on us. 'Control' at p0031. Flag redacted § 11.3 (p0191, 'Following Change in Control of Customer' per TOC) as unreviewable — it may carry a fee.

Customer Data is protected: § 17.1 (p0243) makes us sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data and Confidential Information, with confidentiality/security at p0245-p0250. Deviation risk is deliverables: § 10.4 (p0185) vests in M&I all programs and any work of authorship created in performing the Services 'even if paid for by Customer' (Developed Software), with only a partial refund/credit and a right to resell to other M&I customers; § 17.2 (p0244) limits our rights in M&I software to Term-only use. Position: ownership of, or a perpetual paid-up licence in, custom work we fund.

Only grant is the escrow source-code licence § 23.4 (p0310): non-exclusive, non-transferable, limited to the end of the Term, conditioned on payment of then-current licence fees and on release events (p0311-p0312), with use restrictions § 23.5 (p0313) barring sublicensing (though 'or its designee' appears). § 17.2 (p0244) confines our rights in M&I software to Term-only use; affiliate use addressed indirectly at § 21.10 (p0280). Test: term-limited, fee-conditioned, non-transferable, silent on contractors, and release is not triggered by material breach.

No vendor audit of our usage or licence compliance, so the rule's core risk is absent. Related provisions favour us: § 21.8(C) (p0277) gives a free copy of M&I's annual third-party data-centre review with implementation of recommendations; § 21.8(B) (p0276) and § 17.1 (p0243) preserve regulator/auditor access. Customer-burden points to note only: § 21.8 (p0274) requires us to reimburse M&I's costs of regulatory examinations of our Services, and § 21.7(C)(ii) (p0273) requires evidence of our books-and-records treatment on request.

Direction runs against us: § 13.5 (p0208) has Customer acknowledge both the Termination for Convenience Fee and Termination for Cause Fee as liquidated damages and not a penalty, and both sit outside the § 13.4 cap (p0187, p0189; formula p0039). Credits running to us appear only as § 9.2(D) 'Service Level Credits — REDACTED' (p0177), so the reciprocal benefit is unverifiable — note the redaction. Also note collection fees/Damages (p0149) and default repricing to standard published prices (p0151). Argue quantum once, with T4C.

§ 16.1 (p0231-p0235) gives Term-long warranties: system capability to perform the Services, User Manual conformity, rights/authority, and Millennium Compliance at no additional charge — supported by § 9 Performance Standards (p0155-p0177) and an M&I Event of Default for Performance Standard failure (p0194). Weigh weaknesses: full merchantability/fitness disclaimer § 16.1(F) (p0236); 'commercially reasonable ... no other or higher degree of care' § 9.1 (p0155); 90-day cure for Performance Standard failure (p0194); credits remedy redacted (p0177). Customer reps at § 16.2 (p0237) for symmetry.

Present and robust: § 14.1(A) requires M&I at its own cost throughout the Term to carry CGL of $2,000,000 (p0212-p0213), Fidelity/employee-dishonesty of $10,000,000 across all aspects of the Services (p0214), Workers' Comp with $500,000 Employer's Liability (p0215) and All Risk Property (p0216); § 14.1(B) (p0217) requires A-rated carriers, 30 days' notice of material change or cancellation, and certificates at signing and annually on request. Note as gaps only: no professional liability/E&O and no cyber/privacy cover.

Take-or-pay: § 8.1(ii) (p0130) sets a minimum Monthly Base Fee with volume-based uplifts; § 8.13 (p0149) makes minimum monthly fees payable in advance by ACH debit; § 10.3(A) (p0183) requires us to keep buying every Service in the Monthly Base Fee for the full 8-year Term with no descope right; and the minimum drives the Estimated Remaining Value termination-fee formula (p0039), so the only exit is the T4C fee. Note no-discount and excluded-cost provisions (p0141, p0142, p0146). The missing exit is the material point.

§ 11.4 (p0192) is a genuine Termination Assistance clause: triggered 6 months pre-expiry or on any termination for any reason, all necessary assistance to avoid interruption, transition planning on our schedule, continued Services at contract rates for up to 6 months on 100 days' notice, advance good-faith cost estimate, and no obligation on us to take it. Weigh: all at Customer's expense at M&I's then-current rates, 100-day election notice, 6-month cap, and no express obligation to return or delete Customer Data in a usable format on exit — § 17.1 (p0243) ownership and § 17.5 (p0250) security do not supply a return mechanic. Source-code fallback (p0310, p0313) expires with the Term. 'Effective Date of Termination' at p0038.
